Hi Matthew,

I wanted to send a quick note to thank you again for welcoming us into Jack + Jill for the photo and video shoot. We had a great time, and it was such a pleasure getting to see your team, culture, and operation up close. It's clear you've built something special.

I've also been thinking about our conversations and the growth of wellness, longevity, and peptide programs within aesthetic practices. As you know, this area has become a major focus for many practices across the country, and I'm currently doing some research on the business impact these services have had for established practices.

I'd love to pick your brain and learn more about your experience incorporating peptides into Jack + Jill. Specifically, I'm curious about what your business looked like before introducing peptides versus after, including any impact on revenue, patient retention, recurring revenue, package sales, memberships, or overall patient lifetime value.

Would you be open to grabbing coffee sometime, meeting in person, or jumping on a quick Zoom? This isn't a sales call. I always enjoy learning from operators who are ahead of the curve, and I'd love to hear what's worked, what surprised you, and what you'd do differently if you were starting over.

Neda,

I just have to say, what an incredible time I had filming at your med spa and institute. The space, the energy, your staff, the way you've built everything!  It was genuinely inspiring to be there, and I left feeling so fired up about what you're creating.

I'm so excited to see what's possible between us as we move forward. I think there's a really natural fit for collaboration, and I'd love to explore what that looks like together.

As soon as I get the video edits back, I'll send everything over so you have it ready to use for your socials. I want to make sure you have content that does your space justice.

On another note, I've been working on getting that aesthetic networking group up and running here in the area, and honestly, after seeing your classroom setup, I would absolutely love to entertain hosting one there. It's such a perfect space for it, and I think the community we'd bring together would love it.

Also, I mentioned your situation to a colleague who has experience getting her course CME accredited; she shared some really helpful insight I wanted to pass along. I'm sure you have done your due diligence and already found out most of this, but just in case any of this is helpful I thought I'd pass it along.

She said the smartest starting point for a physician building a training institute is pursuing Joint Providership first. Basically, you partner with an already ACCME-accredited organization to co-deliver your courses under their accreditation umbrella, so your students can earn AMA PRA Category 1 Credits right away without waiting 6 to 10 months for full accreditation. Companies like Global Education Group do exactly this. Once you've built a track record of documented CME activity, usually after a year or two, you apply for full ACCME accreditation directly. The full process involves a self-study report, evidence of performance, and an accreditation interview, and typically takes 6 to 10 months. On the personal credential side, she highly recommended AAAM board certification as the most respected physician-level credential for someone in your position, especially if you want to teach and train with real authority. It's globally recognized and a strong foundation for everything you're building.

Hope this is helpful as you're mapping things out. I'm rooting for you and would love to be part of the journey in whatever way makes sense.

See some attached extras for your use in the meantime.

PROFT INBETWEEN APPOINTMENTS

Also, I have TONS of industry contacts who can help with whatever you need, just let me know your needs! 


Talk soon,
Bethany
